If the model itself is no longer the moat → where does the defensibility come from?
The New Shift: Experience, Ecosystem, and Defaults

Frontier models no longer act as the differentiator they once were.
Everyone ships:
deep research tools
code assistants
voice agents
image/video generation
agentic task runners
Experiences across providers are converging.
Distribution advantage lies with Google, Apple, Microsoft, not OpenAI.
Key insight: If quality converges, the moat must move up the stack.
Why OpenAI Needs a New Moat

First-mover advantage and “best model” advantage were temporary.
The space looks more like industrial economics than software:
High variable compute costs.
Scaling revenue ≠ scaling margins.
Harder for smaller players to compete against distribution giants.
OpenAI needs a moat that:
Reinforces usage,
Reduces switching costs,
And compounds in value over time.
That moat is identity.

Users already treat ChatGPT as “the AI that knows me”
This is the closest thing to a persistent digital self that people have ever used.
AI that knows you becomes irreplaceable if it understands your: context, projects, relationships, taste, habits, working patterns, then switching providers becomes as painful as switching brains.

presenterNotes.177:9472: We had the substance and the drive to write, but we never actually did. WHy is that?
presenterNotes.177:9473: As we dive deeper into the problem, we realized that we’re not alone.
presenterNotes.177:9474: We kept seeing this same friction, in the group of people we started calling “thinkers, not writers” — people rich in ideas but stuck when it comes to sharing them.
presenterNotes.177:9475: What we found is that the issue wasn’t a lack of thoughts, time, or even the right words.
presenterNotes.177:9476: The problem was that writing tools are linear, but our thinking is not.
presenterNotes.177:9477: Thinkers don’t begin with a vision of the piece they want to write.
presenterNotes.177:9478: They begin with a phase of thinking:
presenterNotes.177:9479:
They have domains of interest they actively explore and research
They start spotting interesting ideas within those domains
presenterNotes.177:9482: and explore how to best structure their argument
presenterNotes.177:9483: But in traditional document editors, they only have a blank page and a blinking cursor that demands linear structure from the very start.
presenterNotes.177:9825: Here, every word feels final, exploration feels high-stakes, and editing becomes a loop of undoing. Despite all the ideas in their head, they get stuck at the very first line.
presenterNotes.177:9826: Here’s the paradox: to write, they need structure — but to find structure, they need space to explore.
presenterNotes.177:9827: So that’s the problem we think it’s worth solving and why we built Etch: a thought engine and a playground for thinkers to explore ideas freely and find structure.
